narrative.overview: The Shop makes product discovery easy to scan through clear hierarchy, confident whitespace, and real catalog data. Charcoal navigation anchors the bone-colored reading field; compact Archivo typography and fine rules keep the experience precise without making it feel technical. Product imagery and product names lead wherever real catalog images are available. The spectrum source stays quiet: color is a restrained state signal, not a dashboard language. Storefront navigation, search, category controls, and product links remain familiar web patterns.
keyCharacteristics: Charcoal and bone surfaces with one restrained spectral accent.
Square forms, fine rules, and no decorative elevation.
Familiar controls with explicit, accessible state.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Spectral citron marks an action or selected state; it never becomes a decorative wash across the page.

rules.name: The Product Name Rule
rules.body: Keep names readable before metadata; clamp preview titles to two lines rather than shrinking their type.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Do not add shadows to manufacture hierarchy that spacing, type, or a rule can carry.

dos: Do let product names, prices, categories, and real product images lead.
Do use the doubled marker only to reinforce a selected category.
Do preserve standard storefront navigation and native web control behavior.
Do show an explicit image-unavailable fallback when the API image is absent or is a known placeholder.
donts: Don't turn the storefront into an instrument dashboard or use instrument-specific controls.
Don't invent featured status, popularity, discounts, reviews, or ratings.
Don't substitute unrelated imagery when catalog images are unavailable.
Don't use color as the only indication of selection or focus.
